steps.message:
Dale's comment G-4 wants freeboard dimensioning, sizing calculations and apron details for the emergency spillway on C-9. Before I put the drainage lead on it I need to know whether the spillway as drawn holds up. Work it against the improvement plans and the QA/QC checklist in Design-Drafting, the master drainage study and the storm drain worksheets in Reports-Studies, and the Phase 2 comments and the flood control district acceptance letter in Correspondence/Agency. Tell me whether we can answer G-4 with what's on the sheet today and whether the revisions trigger an amendment to the accepted master study, what the spillway detail and the basin notes have to say on the revised C-9, and where the overflow ends up once it leaves the berm. Put it in a memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026.

Save it as /filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx. Commit to one disposition on each question rather than giving me options. Put units on every value and name the record it comes from. Do not round intermediate values. Work to professional engineering standards.
I'll start by exploring the filesystem to understand the project structure and records.

Project Description

Phase 3 completes the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision by developing the 40.0-acre remainder parcel with 60
lots (half-acre single-family residential), associated public streets, common-area park parcel, streetscape
improvements, storm drain, sanitary sewer and domestic water main extensions from the improvements
constructed under Phases 1 and 2. Phases 1 and 2 (100 lots, 100 acres) were recorded by final map on
12/23/2024 under Map File No. NFM-24-0118 and are built and occupied.

General Notes

    All work shall conform to the current edition of the Clark County Uniform Standard Drawings, the Clark
    County Area Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (Off-Site Improvements), Clark
    County Code Title 30, and the Clark County Public Works Development Review requirements in effect at
    the time of construction.
    All storm drainage design shall conform to the accepted Master Drainage Study — Desert Sage Ranch
    (140 acres), prepared by Sundial Engineering & Survey, Revision 1 dated February 2022, accepted by the
    Clark County Regional Flood Control District by letter dated 02/28/2022. Refer to the master study for
    hydrologic criteria, tributary breakdown, detention allocation by phase, shared outfall allowance and phasing
    exhibit.
    Storage-indication routing under the 100-year, 24-hour design storm governs detention volume; the
    100-year, 6-hour design storm governs storm drain sizing. Rainfall depths applied are 2.38 in. (100-yr, 6-hr)
    and 3.18 in. (100-yr, 24-hr) per the CCRFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual applicable at
    time of master study preparation.
 The Phase 3 gross parcel area of 40.0 acres, at assumed build-out impervious cover of approximately 42%,
discharges to the shared onsite detention basin serving the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision. Phase 3
detention allocation is 6.4 acre-feet per the accepted master drainage study; refer to Sheet C-9 for basin
geometry, cross-sections and weir details.
The shared outfall serving the full 140-acre subdivision is located at the southwest corner of the parent
parcel and is subject to a Q100 cap of 78 cfs per the master drainage study. Phase 3 does not compute a
phase-specific outfall discharge; contribution is routed through the shared onsite detention system.
Boundary geometry, monumentation and horizontal control shown on Sheets C-2 and C-3 are based on the
recorded final map for Phases 1 and 2 (Map File No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175 of Plats, Page 60, recorded
12/23/2024, Clark County Recorder Instrument No. 20241223-0004421) for the north boundary of the
Phase 3 remainder parcel, and on the approved Tentative Map TM-22-500041 for the interior geometry and
street layout.
Basis of Bearings: N 89°57'42" E, being the bearing of the south line of the Southwest Quarter of Section
27, T. 22 S., R. 60 E., M.D.M., Clark County, Nevada, per the recorded Phase 1–2 final map. All bearings
and distances shown are grid, Nevada State Plane Coordinate System, East Zone (NAD 83/94, HARN),
ground-to-grid combined factor 1.00006428.
Datum: Elevations shown are NAVD 88, established by GPS observation to Clark County vertical control
station "SEC-27-1" (found brass-cap monument at the South Quarter Corner of Section 27), elevation
2,852.14 ft.
Contours shown on grading sheets are drawn at 1-foot intervals. Spot elevations to two decimal places.
Zoning: R-2 (Medium Density Residential). No portion of the Phase 3 parcel lies within a designated
floodway. Property lies within FEMA FIRM Panel 32003C 3960 G (effective 11/16/2011), Zone X (areas of
minimal flood hazard).
Domestic water and fire flow service to be provided by the Las Vegas Valley Water District (LVVWD) per
will-serve letter dated 07/22/2026. Sanitary sewer service to be provided by the Clark County Water
Reclamation District (CCWRD). Wet utility plans by others under separate cover; interface with grading and
storm drain shown herein.
Dry utility joint trench (electric, gas, telecommunications) by others under separate cover; see Dry Utility
Composite Plan for coordination.
Existing improvements constructed under Phases 1 and 2 are shown for reference only. Phase 2 storm
drain stub at the common phase boundary is to be extended into Phase 3 as shown on Sheet C-8. Refer to
Phase 2 as-built record drawings for stub invert and pipe size.
All streets within Phase 3 are to be dedicated to Clark County for public use under the Phase 3 final map
(FM-26-100290) to be presented for recordation following approval of these improvement plans.
All common-area landscape strips, entry monument, park parcel and private drainage facilities are to be
owned and maintained by the Desert Sage Ranch Community Association in accordance with the
recorded CC&Rs. The Phase 3 HOA park identified on these civil sheets as Common-Area Parcel "D"
corresponds to the common-area park referenced as Parcel A on the Phase 3 landscape sheets (L-1
through L-4) and in the CC&Rs; the two designations refer to the same physical parcel.
Contractor shall notify Underground Service Alert of Nevada (USA North 811) a minimum of two (2) working
days prior to any excavation.
Construction stormwater discharge shall be conducted under coverage of NDEP General Permit
NVR100000, Construction Stormwater. Contractor shall maintain the approved SWPPP onsite at all times
during construction and file the Notice of Termination upon final stabilization.
All dimensions shown are in U.S. Survey Feet and decimal parts thereof.
Legend and abbreviations used on Sheets C-2 through C-9 appear at right on this sheet. P.U.E. = Public

                         1. INTRODUCTION AND PROJECT DESCRIPTION


1.1 Purpose

The purpose of this Master Drainage Study is to establish the hydrologic and hydraulic basis of design for storm
drainage improvements serving the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision, a 140-acre residential development to be
constructed in three phases in the Enterprise area of unincorporated Clark County, Nevada. This study is
submitted to the Clark County Regional Flood Control District (CCRFCD) for acceptance and, upon acceptance,
is intended to serve as the master planning document governing all subsequent improvement plan submittals for
the individual phases.



1.2 Project Location

Desert Sage Ranch occupies a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., in
unincorporated Clark County. The site is bounded generally by Rainbow Boulevard on the west and Windmill
Lane on the south, with the project address of record identified as Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las
Vegas, Nevada 89178. Assessor Parcel Number 177-27-201-001 encompasses the balance of the site not
already partitioned.

The site is located within the Enterprise Town Advisory Board area of unincorporated Clark County and is
governed by Clark County Code Title 30. Land use planning oversight is exercised by Clark County
Comprehensive Planning.



1.3 Site Description and Development

The 140-acre site is generally undeveloped desert terrain sloping gently from the northeast to the southwest at
an average grade of approximately 1.6 percent. Native ground cover consists of sparse creosote and bursage
on gravelly, well-drained soils overlying a caliche-influenced subsurface typical of the Enterprise sub-basin.
There are no defined natural watercourses across the site; historic runoff sheet-flows to the southwest.

Desert Sage Ranch will be developed as a single-family residential subdivision served by public streets. Phase
3 consists of 60 half-acre lots (100 ft × 220 ft, approximately 22,000 sf); Phases 1 and 2 consist of smaller
residential lots (approximately 6,050 sf, 55 ft × 110 ft) per the recorded Phase 1-2 Final Map. The full 140 acres
will be built out in three sequential phases:

    • Phase 1 — 45.0 acres, northern portion of the site.
    • Phase 2 — 55.0 acres, central portion of the site.
    • Phase 3 — 40.0 acres, southern portion of the site, comprising 60 half-acre lots and associated street
    frontage, HOA common-area park and streetscape improvements.

Each phase will be constructed under its own improvement plan set, prepared to be consistent with this Master
Drainage Study.
 1.4 Regulatory Framework

This study has been prepared in conformance with:

    • Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, edition
    applicable at the time of preparation;
    • Clark County Uniform Standard Drawings and applicable Public Works standards;
    • Clark County Code Title 30 (development standards).

Hydrologic and hydraulic methods, precipitation input, loss rates and detention criteria are drawn from the
CCRFCD manual as it stood at the time of study preparation and acceptance. Subsequent phase-level design
shall comply with the master allocations set forth herein.



1.5 Study Deliverables

This document establishes:

    • Design storm criteria and rainfall depths.
    • Tributary-area delineation for the full 140 acres, broken down by development phase.
    • Peak discharge estimates for the tributary sub-basins under fully developed conditions.
    • A shared onsite detention approach with a fixed allocation of storage volume to each phase.
    • Allowance for the full 140 acres at a shared outfall to the downstream regional facility, with a maximum
    permitted discharge.
    • A phasing exhibit identifying phase boundaries and detention basin locations.



                       2. EXISTING CONDITIONS AND OFFSITE TRIBUTARY


2.1 Topography and Soils

Existing topography across the 140-acre site is a gently sloping desert plain. Elevations range from
approximately 2,905 feet at the northeast corner to approximately 2,850 feet at the southwest outfall point,
yielding an average site slope of approximately 1.6 percent to the southwest.

Surface soils across the site are classified as SM to SP-SM (silty sands and poorly graded sands with silt), with
cemented caliche horizons at variable depth. Infiltration rates in the caliche zone are low, and no percolation
credit is taken in the hydrologic analysis. The full computed runoff volume is treated as surface flow for the
purposes of this study.



2.2 Existing Drainage Pattern

Under existing conditions, stormwater sheet-flows overland from north-northeast to south-southwest across the
site. There are no defined channels within the property boundaries. At the southwest corner of the site, runoff
 historically discharges toward the downstream regional drainage facility maintained by CCRFCD.



2.3 Offsite Tributary from the North

The site accepts a modest offsite drainage flow entering along the northern boundary of what will become Phase
1. The offsite tributary area upstream of the north boundary consists of approximately 38 acres of low-density
residential and open desert land. Under fully developed offsite conditions consistent with the surrounding land
use plan, the offsite peak inflow at the northern site boundary has been estimated as summarized in Section 3
and Appendix C.

The offsite tributary flow enters the site as sheet flow along the northern boundary and, at build-out, will be
conveyed through the Phase 1 street network to the shared onsite detention basin(s). No offsite bypass channel
is proposed; the accepted offsite flow is passed through the onsite storm drain and routed through detention
along with the onsite runoff.



2.4 Downstream Conveyance

The shared onsite outfall is located at the southwest corner of the property and discharges to the downstream
regional CCRFCD facility via an existing reinforced concrete pipe stub set during earlier regional construction.
The receiving facility has been reviewed against the shared outfall allowance identified in Section 5; downstream
capacity is not the controlling constraint for the site's release rate. The controlling constraint is the outfall
allowance established for Desert Sage Ranch and set forth in this study.

    • 100-year, 24-hour storm — used for detention basin sizing (governing storage volume).

 3.2 Method

Rainfall-runoff modeling was performed using CCRFCD-accepted methods appropriate for a subdivision of this
size, applying the Green-Ampt infiltration approach for pervious surfaces and directly-connected impervious
modeling for developed areas. Sub-basin delineation follows the tributary breakdown described in Section 3.3.
Routing to and through the shared detention basin(s) was performed using the storage-indication method.

Impervious cover assumed at build-out reflects the approved half-acre residential lot type with associated street
and driveway coverage, streetscape landscape strips, and HOA common-area park.

                                          4. DETENTION SIZING


4.1 Shared Onsite Detention Approach

Desert Sage Ranch is served by a shared onsite detention approach: the detention volume required to attenuate
the site's peak discharge to the accepted outfall release rate is provided in shared onsite detention facilities
 constructed as the subdivision phases advance. Detention basin locations are identified on the phasing exhibit
(Section 6).

The shared approach avoids duplication of small phase-scale basins and consolidates operations and
maintenance for the HOA. Because the phases share the same outfall and downstream facility, the storage
requirement has been determined for the fully developed 140-acre site and then allocated among the three
phases in accordance with the acreage and impervious cover of each phase.



4.2 Governing Design Storm

Storage sizing is governed by the 100-year, 24-hour design storm. The 100-year, 6-hour storm is used to check
peak discharge to the shared basin(s) and storm drain sizing, but does not govern storage. Storage-indication
routing under the 100-year, 24-hour storm, with the outfall released at the allowance identified in Section 5,
produces a total site-wide required storage volume of 16.4 acre-feet.



4.3 Detention Allocation by Phase

Total storage required for the fully developed 140-acre site is allocated to the three phases on the basis of
tributary runoff volume and position in the shared outfall, not by pro-rata acreage. Phase 3 discharges last
and carries the largest attenuation duty; volumes were reviewed and fixed at District acceptance, and are
the fixed planning basis for subsequent phase-level submittals.

                                                  5. OUTFALL


5.1 Shared Outfall

The full 140-acre Desert Sage Ranch subdivision discharges to the downstream regional CCRFCD facility
through a single shared outfall located at the southwest corner of the site. The outfall discharges via an existing
reinforced concrete pipe stub previously installed by others as part of regional drainage construction.
Confirmation of downstream capacity has been obtained from the District as part of this study's review.



5.2 Allowance and Cap

An allowance for the full 140 acres at the shared outfall to the downstream regional facility has been established
for Desert Sage Ranch, subject to the following cap:

Q100 ≤ 78 cfs at the shared outfall.

The 78 cfs cap represents the maximum permitted 100-year peak discharge from the fully developed 140-acre
site into the receiving regional facility. Storage-indication routing through the shared onsite detention basin(s) as
sized in Section 4 attenuates the fully developed peak inflow at the basin(s) to a peak release at or below the 78
cfs cap.



5.3 Application to Phase-Level Plans

Because the cap applies to the shared outfall for the full 140-acre site — not to any single phase — phase-level
improvement plan sets are not to compute a phase-specific outfall discharge. Each phase's contribution is
routed into the shared detention system, and the shared outfall discharge remains subject to the 78 cfs cap at
build-out.

                                               7. CONCLUSION


7.1 Summary

This Master Drainage Study establishes the hydrologic and hydraulic basis of design for the 140-acre Desert
Sage Ranch subdivision. The study:

    • adopts the 100-year, 6-hour and 100-year, 24-hour design storms in accordance with the CCRFCD
    Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual applicable at time of preparation;
    • delineates tributary areas for the full 140 acres, broken down by the three development phases;
    • establishes a shared onsite detention approach with fixed volume allocations by phase — Phase 1 at 4.2
    acre-feet, Phase 2 at 5.8 acre-feet, Phase 3 at 6.4 acre-feet, and total site at 16.4 acre-feet;
    • confirms an allowance for the full 140 acres at the shared outfall to the downstream regional facility,
    capped at Q100 = 78 cfs;
    • provides a phasing exhibit identifying phase boundaries, detention basin locations, offsite tributary corridor
    and shared outfall.


7.2 Basis for Subsequent Design

Upon CCRFCD acceptance, this Master Drainage Study serves as the master planning document for all
subsequent improvement plan submittals for Desert Sage Ranch, including but not limited to Phase 1, Phase 2
and Phase 3 grading and drainage plan sets and their supporting hydrology, storm drain and detention
worksheets. Phase-level design shall be consistent with the tributary breakdown, detention allocation by phase,
and shared outfall allowance identified herein.



7.3 Amendments

Changes to the accepted detention allocations set forth in Table 4-1, the outfall allowance set forth in Section 5,
or the tributary breakdown and phase boundaries set forth in Sections 3 and 6, require formal amendment to this
study and re-review by the Clark County Regional Flood Control District. Phase-level improvement plans that
propose to depart from the accepted allocations or allowance shall be preceded by an accepted amendment; no
phase-level plan set shall be approved on the basis of a departure that has not been separately submitted to
and accepted by the District.

The CCRFCD acceptance letter dated February 28, 2022 (Appendix F) confirms this requirement and is
incorporated herein by reference.

Phases 1–2 Final Map Job / File: TM-22-500041 (parent); IP-22-100156 (Phase 2 Improvement Plans);
FM-22-100158 (Phases 1–2 Final Map) Submittal received: August 15, 2022 Applicant / Engineer of Record:

Mr. Braddock:

Development Review has completed the first-round plan check of the referenced Phase 2 Improvement Plans
and the accompanying Phases 1–2 Final Map. Comments follow in two sections:

    • General Comments are binding and must be addressed prior to plan approval. Return a response column
    against each item at resubmittal.
    • Advisory Comments identify items that will benefit the plan but are not, by themselves, cause for holding
    approval. Confirm intent at resubmittal.

Comments are grouped by discipline and numbered within discipline (e.g., G-1, U-1, M-1, F-1, L-1). All sheet
references are to the submittal received August 15, 2022. Where a comment lists more than one sheet, the
response shall address each occurrence.



                                          GENERAL COMMENTS


Grading and Drainage (G)

G-1. Sheets C-2 through C-4: Provide a project-wide contour interval statement in the general notes and confirm
that spot elevations shown at the north property boundary tie to Phase 3 concept grades within ±0.10 ft.
Boundary conditions at the future Phase 3 line shall be shown as "future match — see Phase 3 improvement
plans" and dimensioned from the recorded lot line.

G-2. Sheet C-2, Detention Basin DB-2: The basin outlet structure detail (Detail 4/C-8) does not match the sizing
indicated in the drainage study. Reconcile the orifice diameter and weir crest elevation between the plan sheet,
the detail, and Table 3 of the master drainage study prepared for the tentative map. Provide corrected detail with
revision cloud.

G-3. Sheets C-3 and C-4: Show the 100-year water surface elevation and freeboard at each detention basin on
plan. Freeboard shall be a minimum of 1.0 ft above the design HGL and shall be dimensioned.

G-4. Sheet C-3: Add cross-lot drainage arrows on Lots 22–31 where finish-floor differentials exceed 2.5 ft.
Provide swale sections at typical locations and reference the swale detail on Sheet C-8.
 G-5. Sheet C-4: Storm drain pipe SD-14 is shown crossing the proposed sanitary sewer main between MH-8
and MH-9. Verify the vertical separation and provide a crossing detail with clearances called out. Note in the
profile view that the sewer is the lower utility and shall be encased where separation is less than 18 inches.

G-6. Sheet C-5: Pavement section for the private drives does not match the geotechnical report
recommendation of 3.0" AC over 6.0" ATB over 12" Type II. Confirm the pavement callout and add a reference
to the geotechnical report of record.

G-7. Sheet C-8, Detail 2 (curb and gutter): Reference the current Clark County Uniform Standard Drawing
number and confirm dimensions. The 6" vertical curb detail as shown does not match Standard Drawing No.
200.1.

G-8. Provide a signed and sealed drainage certification statement on the cover sheet in the standard form ("I
hereby certify that the drainage design conforms to the approved master drainage study for Desert Sage
Ranch…"). The engineer's seal shall be signed at plan approval, not on the review copy.



Utilities (U)

U-1. Sheet C-6, water plan: Fire hydrant spacing along "A" Street exceeds 500 ft between HYD-04 and HYD-05.
Add an intermediate hydrant or demonstrate compliance with the local water purveyor spacing table. Coordinate
with LVVWD prior to resubmittal.

U-2. Sheet C-6: Show the connection to the existing 12" transmission main on Windmill Lane with a call-out for
the wet tap, valve, and thrust restraint. Provide the wet tap detail (LVVWD Standard) on Sheet C-9.

U-3. Sheet C-7, sanitary sewer plan: Sanitary sewer profile between MH-12 and MH-13 shows a slope of 0.38%.
Minimum design slope for an 8" main is 0.40%. Revise to meet CCWRD Design and Construction Standards. If
the profile constraint is a boundary condition to future Phase 3, note this at MH-13 as a "stub for future Phase 3
extension" and coordinate the invert with the Phase 3 concept.

U-4. Sheet C-7: The manhole schedule (Schedule 2, Sheet C-9) is missing rim and invert elevations for MH-9
and MH-14. Provide.

U-5. Dry utility joint trench: The composite dry utility plan referenced on the cover sheet was not included in the
submittal package. Provide the joint-trench composite plan showing NV Energy, Southwest Gas, telephone, and
cable, with clearances to wet utilities. Confirm that the 20-foot dry utility easement shown along the north (future
Phase 3) boundary matches the easement dimensioned on the final map.



Mapping (M)

M-1. Final map Sheet 1, Owner's Certificate and Dedication: The dedication language does not include the
standard easement dedication for "public utility, drainage, sewer and access easements as shown on this map."
Revise the certificate wording to the Clark County template on file with the County Surveyor.

M-2. Final map Sheet 1, Notary acknowledgment: The Nevada notary acknowledgment shall be the
"all-purpose" form with a stated county of acknowledgment. The submitted form omits the county line. Correct.

M-3. Final map Sheet 2: The Basis of Bearings statement is set as N 00°00'00" E along the west line of Section
27. Provide the record of survey or filed map reference from which the basis is taken, in the standard form.
 M-4. Final map Sheet 3: A 20-foot dry utility easement is called out along the north boundary of the Phase 3
remainder but is not dimensioned from the section line. Add the perpendicular offset and confirm the width at
each break point.

M-5. Final map Sheet 3, lot dimensions: Lot 47 closes with an unbalanced traverse of 0.06 ft. Adjust the
least-squares closure or the boundary bearing and resubmit the closure sheet.

M-6. Final map Sheet 4: Provide the recorder's note per N.R.S. 278.5695 in the standard form. Confirm the filing
block leaves room for book and page reference to be entered at recordation.



Fire Access (F)

F-1. Sheet C-2: The turnaround at the west end of "C" Street is shown as a hammerhead with a 60-ft throat.
Confirm dimensions against the current Clark County Fire Department (CCFD) Fire Code Amendments and
provide the CCFD-standard turnaround detail on Sheet C-9. Aerial apparatus access from the hammerhead to
Lots 51–56 shall be shown by clear line-of-approach.

F-2. Sheet C-2 and Sheet C-4: The plan shows a temporary construction stub extending north from the
terminus of "B" Street across the future Phase 3 parcel to Windmill Lane, labeled "Temporary Secondary
Access — Phase 2 Only." The improvement is graded, base-coursed and provided with a 26-ft aggregate driving
surface and turnouts. Development Review notes that (i) the stub crosses ground that is not part of the Phase 2
final map area, and (ii) the plan sheet does not indicate the mechanism by which the access is legally
established (temporary construction easement, license, or dedicated access) or the date/event on which it
expires. A formal Clark County Fire Department review and written determination is required regarding
the temporary vs. permanent designation of this access, the acceptable duration of the temporary condition,
and the trigger for its removal or conversion to a permanent facility. Refer to CCFD for a stand-alone letter.
Coordinate resubmittal timing with CCFD so that the fire access determination is on record before final map
recordation.

F-3. Sheet C-6, fire hydrant locations: Two hydrants (HYD-02 and HYD-07) fall outside the 400-ft hose-lay
coverage envelope for Lots 8 and 33 respectively. Relocate, or add hydrants, to bring all lots within the required
coverage. Show the hose-lay envelope on the water plan for review.



Landscape (L)

L-1. Sheet L-1: The street tree schedule for "A" Street and Windmill Lane frontage shows a mixed palette of
desert-adapted species (Prosopis chilensis, Acacia stenophylla, Chilopsis linearis). Provide caliper size and root
barrier detail. Root barriers shall be provided where trees are within 5 ft of sidewalks or curbs. Reference the
standard root barrier detail on Sheet L-3.

L-2. Sheet L-2, common-area park plan: Provide plant quantities in a summary schedule and confirm that the
shade tree count over the designated play area meets the Title 30 canopy target. Add the standard general note
that the HOA is responsible for common-area landscape maintenance in perpetuity.



                                         ADVISORY COMMENTS

A-1. The cover sheet vicinity map is at a scale that makes the section/township/range hard to read. Consider a
larger inset for clarity.
 A-2. Recommend adding a general note referencing the approved master drainage study by title, date, and
preparer on the cover sheet, in addition to the certification called for in G-8.

A-3. For readability, the sanitary sewer profile (Sheet C-7) would benefit from a break at MH-11 rather than the
current single continuous scale run. Optional.

A-4. Consider labelling the future Phase 3 boundary on Sheet C-2 with an explanatory note ("Phase 3 not part of
this submittal — see future improvement plans") to avoid confusion during construction inspection.

A-5. The joint trench composite (see U-5) may be submitted as a separate exhibit rather than an additional plan
sheet if that is preferred by the dry utility coordinator.


Resubmit the plan set and final map with a response column indicating action taken against each numbered
general comment, together with any revised sheets clouded and triangled. Advisory comments do not require a
written response but any changes taken in response to them shall be clouded.

Direct questions on this letter to the undersigned.

[Normal] 1. Attendees
[Normal] Callaway Land Partners was invited but did not attend; Max Braddock represented applicant-side coordination.
[Normal] 2. Purpose
[Normal] Pre-application discussion of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement plan and final map resubmittal package under the current code cycle. Objective was to align the design team and County reviewers on submittal composition, review path, and any threshold issues that ought to be flagged before intake, so the package can move through Public Works plan check on the first submittal without a routing surprise.
[Normal] Phase 3 is the final 40.0 acres (60 half-acre lots) of the 140-acre subdivision entitled under Tentative Map TM-22-500041 (approved 03/14/2022). Phases 1 and 2 are built and occupied; the first final map in the series was recorded in 2024.
[Normal] 3. Topics Discussed
[Normal] 3.1 Submittal package composition and application numbers. Max walked through the intended package. County has already issued application numbers on the intake pre-check:
[List Bullet] Improvement Plans: IP-26-100288
[List Bullet] Final Map: FM-26-100290
[Normal] Package as contemplated for first submittal:
[List Bullet] Improvement plan set (grading, drainage, streets, wet/dry utility composite) — Sundial
[List Bullet] Landscape and irrigation set — Ocotillo Landscape Studio
[List Bullet] Final Map (three-sheet, second in the TM-22-500041 series) — Sundial Survey
[List Bullet] Supporting reports: updated drainage narrative referencing the approved master drainage study; geotechnical addendum; traffic memo confirming trip generation is unchanged from tentative-map assumptions
[List Bullet] Title report and closure package — Callaway to procure through Silver Butte Title & Escrow
[List Bullet] Agency will-serve / capacity confirmations from LVVWD and CCWRD (see 3.5)
[Normal] Dale Yeoman confirmed the two application numbers above are the correct references and should appear on the title block and cover sheets of every submitted sheet. He asked that IP-26-100288 be cited on the drainage narrative title page as well.
[Normal] 3.2 Drainage — master study governs. Priya summarized the drainage approach: Phase 3 drains to the detention basin sized under the approved master drainage study for the subdivision. Detention allocation for Phase 3 was fixed in that study; there are no departures anticipated in the resubmittal.
[Normal] Dale confirmed that so long as the Phase 3 improvement plans match the volumes and outfall configuration in the district-approved master drainage study, no fresh hydrology submittal to Regional Flood Control is required — a narrative-level reconciliation in the drainage report is sufficient. He noted plan check will still verify the basin geometry against the study.
[Normal] Priya to include a reconciliation table (basin volume as built into Phase 1/2, allocations for Phase 3, and headroom) in the drainage narrative.
[Normal] 3.3 Landscape — significant-change threshold. Bea Cortland summarized the landscape approach: streetscape palette carried forward from the approved 2022 Phase 1/2 palette (desert planting throughout streetscapes; turf confined to the HOA common-area park). Species list is substantially the same as Phase 1/2. Some substitutions in the shrub layer may be proposed as availability has shifted since 2022.
[Normal] Odette Marchetti raised that any landscape changes from the approved 2022 palette may require review beyond staff level depending on extent — the significant-change threshold has to be evaluated on the actual proposed change. She referenced condition 14 of the tentative map approval letter, which contemplates design review as a public hearing before the Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission for significant changes to approved plans, including landscape and streetscape treatments in common areas.
[Normal] Discussion did not resolve where the significant-change threshold sits for this project. Odette noted the evaluation is fact-specific and that the design team should provide a red-line comparison of the proposed Phase 3 palette against the 2022 approved palette so Planning can make that call once the actual proposed change is on paper. Bea agreed to prepare that comparison as part of the landscape resubmittal.
[Normal] No commitment was made at the meeting as to whether the resubmittal will or will not trigger design review. The point was flagged for the team's awareness; a written determination from Planning would follow the submittal.
[Normal] 3.4 Fire access. Lt. Salazar (attending for Capt. Roark) noted that the CCFD review will focus on the permanent buildout access configuration for Phase 3. The temporary secondary access accepted at Phase 2 buildout was approved as a temporary condition pending Phase 3 development, and Phase 3 improvement plans need to show the permanent second point of access consistent with the tentative map. Any deviation from what was shown on TM-22-500041 should be pre-coordinated with Capt. Roark before submittal.
[Normal] Sundial to circulate the current Phase 3 access layout to CCFD in advance of the formal submittal for informal review; the substantive determination on the permanent buildout condition will come from CCFD through the plan check letter.
[Normal] 3.5 Utilities. K. Odhiambo confirmed that separate confirmations from Las Vegas Valley Water District (LVVWD) and Clark County Water Reclamation District (CCWRD) will be needed for the resubmittal package. These are separate agency confirmations obtained by the applicant/engineer directly with each district; the County does not procure them.
[Normal] Noted for the record; no further discussion.
[Normal] 3.6 SWPPP / grading permit sequencing. Priya asked about sequencing between improvement plan approval and the grading permit / SWPPP. Dale confirmed the standard sequence:
[List Number] Improvement plans routed and approved (IP-26-100288)
[List Number] NDEP Bureau of Water Pollution Control NOI filed by contractor; SWPPP prepared under NPDES general construction permit
[List Number] Grading permit application submitted to Public Works with the SWPPP and approved improvement plans referenced
[List Number] Grading permit issued once bonds/estimate are posted through Callaway
[Normal] The grading permit cannot issue ahead of improvement plan approval. Dale mentioned that Callaway will need to have the surety and cost estimate lined up on the Public Works side before grading permit issuance, but that this is not a first-submittal item.
[Normal] 4. Agreed Submittal Route
[Normal] The resubmittal will be routed through Clark County Public Works, Development Review, with Comprehensive Planning coordination on the landscape and final map conditions. Dale Yeoman is the assigned civil plans examiner (Public Works). Odette Marchetti is the point of contact on the Comprehensive Planning side for the tentative map conditions carry-forward and the significant-change evaluation.
[Normal] Public Works will circulate the improvement plans internally to CCFD and Landscape review. Applicant is responsible for obtaining LVVWD and CCWRD confirmations separately (see 3.5) and including them in the submittal package.
[Normal] Formal intake will be at the Public Works counter under application numbers IP-26-100288 (improvement plans) and FM-26-100290 (final map).

[Normal] Distribution of these notes: attendees above, plus CCFD Fire Plans Examiner (Capt. Emmett Roark) and Sundial project file 2201-03.
[Normal] 2.  County Submittal and Inspection Sequence
[Normal] The construction inspection sequence was walked through by Terrence Kolb (Clark County Public Works — Development Review). The following items were agreed and will govern Phase 2 inspection administration:
[Normal] 2.1  Inspection request procedure.
[Normal] Mesquite Basin will submit inspection requests through the County Public Works construction inspection portal not less than 48 hours in advance of the requested inspection window. Requests will cite the improvement plan sheet, station range, and item to be inspected. Sundial's field engineer will be copied on each request; where the field engineer's presence is required (e.g., subgrade acceptance, storm drain pressure test, pavement structural section) Sundial will attend jointly with the County inspector.
[Normal] 2.2  Progressive inspections during construction.
[Normal] Phase 2 will be inspected on a rolling basis by item: rough grading and moisture-density; storm drain trench, bedding and pressure tests prior to backfill; curb-and-gutter forming; subbase; base; and pavement placement. County inspector will sign each item on County inspection form; Sundial will maintain the running set of signed reports in the construction record for Phase 2.
[Normal] 2.3  Pre-final inspection.
[Normal] When the improvements listed on the approved plans are complete in the field — including punch-list-condition landscape, signing and striping, and the temporary construction stub at the north boundary as shown on the improvement plans — Callaway will submit a written request for pre-final inspection. County will schedule the pre-final walk within ten (10) working days of the request. Sundial and Mesquite Basin will attend. Any punch items identified will be logged on the County form on-site and returned to Callaway the same week.
[Normal] 2.4  Final inspection and acceptance.
[Normal] Following completion of pre-final punch, Callaway will submit a written request for final inspection with a signed contractor statement that punch items are complete. County will schedule final inspection within ten (10) working days. On satisfactory final inspection, County Public Works will issue a written improvement acceptance letter under separate cover. It was noted that Phase 2 offsite improvements (Rainbow Blvd. frontage, curb return at Windmill Ln., traffic control device) may be finalled and accepted on a schedule independent of the onsite balance; the two acceptances will be handled as separate letters. This is consistent with the release provisions in the Phase 2 improvement agreement and performance bond.
[Normal] 2.5  Record drawings.
[Normal] Sundial will prepare Phase 2 record drawings (as-builts) from contractor red-lines, field survey, and County inspection reports, for submission with the improvement acceptance package. Sundial will maintain a working red-line set at the trailer for the duration of construction; the general contractor will keep a mirrored set. Record drawings will be sealed and dated after final inspection.
[Normal] 3.  Traffic Control and Access
[Normal] 3.1  Construction access — primary.
[Normal] Primary construction ingress and egress for Phase 2 will be from Rainbow Blvd. at the approved Phase 2 entry throat. All haul routes into and out of the site will use this entry. A traffic control plan conforming to the MUTCD and Clark County Public Works standards has been submitted by Mesquite Basin and approved for the Rainbow Blvd. work zone (curb return, taper, and flagger station).
[Normal] 3.2  Temporary construction stub across undeveloped Phase 3.
[Normal] A temporary construction stub will be graded and paved across the northern boundary of the built Phase 2 area, extending into and across the presently undeveloped Phase 3 parcel to tie back to Windmill Ln. This stub is called out on the approved improvement plans and shown on the traffic control exhibit distributed at the meeting.
[Normal] Two uses of the stub were confirmed and agreed:
[List Bullet] Construction traffic.  The stub will serve as a secondary construction access for material deliveries and heavy equipment during Phase 2 construction, relieving the Rainbow Blvd. entry.
[List Bullet] Secondary emergency access for occupied Phase 2.  Once dwelling units in Phase 2 are occupied and while Phase 3 remains undeveloped ground, the stub will serve as the secondary point of access required by CCFD for Phase 2 emergency response.
[Normal] Both uses are expressly temporary. The stub crosses ground that is planned for Phase 3 subdivision development. It exists only because the Phase 3 remainder is presently ungraded and open. When Phase 3 is developed the stub will be removed and superseded by whatever access configuration is approved for Phase 3 on its own merits. This limitation was discussed in the meeting and was subsequently confirmed in writing by CCFD.
[Normal] CCFD approval status.
[Normal] At the time of the meeting, the CCFD access approval for Phase 2 was under review. Following the meeting, CCFD issued its formal approval by letter dated 06/12/2023 (Capt. Emmett Roark, Fire Plans Examiner). The letter approves the secondary access configuration for Phase 2 as a temporary condition pending development of Phase 3. That temporary designation is acknowledged on the record. Callaway and Sundial will maintain the CCFD letter in the project record and will treat the stub as a Phase 2 arrangement only; nothing in the CCFD Phase 2 correspondence is to be read as approval of an access configuration for Phase 3.
[Normal] 3.3  Stub construction and maintenance.
[Normal] Mesquite Basin will construct the stub to the section and alignment shown on the approved Phase 2 improvement plans (compacted aggregate base with a bituminous surface course of the section noted on Sheet C-6). The stub will be barricaded at the Phase 3-side terminus with a Type III barricade and CCFD-compliant emergency-access knock-down gate. The stub will be maintained by Callaway for the duration of Phase 2 occupancy and until Phase 3 construction commences. Weekly inspection of the stub surface and barricade will be logged by Mesquite Basin during construction and by Callaway/HOA thereafter.
[Normal] 3.4  Signage.
[Normal] "Emergency Access Only — No Public Through-Access" signage will be posted at the stub in both directions, per CCFD sign schedule. Contractor construction-access signage will be posted separately during the construction period only.
[Normal] 4.  BMP Installation Sequence per SWPPP
[Normal] The project Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), as authored by Sundial and covered under the NDEP General Permit NVR100000 Notice of Intent for Desert Sage Ranch, governs installation and sequencing of construction stormwater BMPs. The following sequence was walked and agreed on-site:
[Normal] 4.1  Prior to any grading disturbance.
[Normal] The following perimeter and inlet-protection BMPs will be installed and inspected before any Phase 2 earthwork begins:
[List Bullet] Silt fence and reinforced silt fence along the downgradient (south and west) perimeter of the Phase 2 disturbance area, as shown on the SWPPP site map.
[List Bullet] Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad with wheel-wash provision) at the Rainbow Blvd. primary construction entry.
[List Bullet] Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad) at the temporary stub terminus at Windmill Ln.
[List Bullet] Inlet protection (sandbag berm or filter insert) at all existing off-site catch basins within 100 ft of the disturbance boundary along Rainbow Blvd. and Windmill Ln.
[List Bullet] Concrete washout containment at the location shown on the SWPPP site map, off the primary construction entry.
[Normal] Sundial's field engineer will walk the perimeter BMPs with Mesquite Basin's superintendent and sign the SWPPP inspection log the day the perimeter is complete and before earthwork disturbance begins.
[Normal] 4.2  During mass grading.
[Normal] Track-out control at both construction entries will be inspected daily by Mesquite Basin and after each significant rainfall event. Wind-erosion control (application of water and, where directed, tackifier) will follow the schedule in the SWPPP and the requirements of the Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability dust control permit for the site.
[Normal] 4.3  As storm drain becomes operational.
[Normal] As Phase 2 catch basins are installed, inlet protection (gravel bag or filter fabric type as noted in the SWPPP) will be placed at each basin the same day the frame and grate are set. Protection will remain in place until final stabilization or until paving is complete, whichever is later.
[Normal] 4.4  Stabilization.
[Normal] Temporary stabilization of disturbed areas that will remain inactive for more than fourteen (14) days will be by application of tackifier or hydromulch, per the SWPPP. Final stabilization will be by landscape installation in improved areas and by soil binder / gravel treatment on Phase-2-facing slopes of the Phase 3 remainder that are disturbed by grading of the temporary stub.
[Normal] 4.5  Inspections and records.
[Normal] Mesquite Basin will conduct SWPPP inspections weekly and within 24 hours after any rainfall of 0.25 inch or greater, log each inspection on the SWPPP inspection form, and correct deficiencies within the timeframes specified in the SWPPP. Sundial will spot-audit inspections at not less than a monthly interval. All SWPPP records will be kept at the site trailer and available for review by NDEP or Clark County inspectors.
[Normal] 4.6  Notice of Termination.
[Normal] When Phase 2 improvements reach final stabilization and the improvements are accepted, Sundial will prepare and file a Notice of Termination with NDEP under NVR100000 to close construction stormwater coverage for the Phase 2 area of disturbance. The Notice of Termination will be limited to the Phase 2 area of disturbance and will be filed in the project record.
[Normal] 5.  Utility Coordination
[Normal] 5.1  Wet utilities.
[List Bullet] Water.  Water main installation is by Mesquite Basin under LVVWD standard specifications, on the alignments and to the sizes shown on the approved plans. Pressure test and disinfection to LVVWD standards; LVVWD field acceptance required prior to service connection. LVVWD inspector to be scheduled by Mesquite Basin through the LVVWD construction desk with 48-hour notice.
[List Bullet] Sewer.  Sewer main installation is by Mesquite Basin under CCWRD standard specifications. Mandrel test and low-pressure air test on completed reaches; CCWRD field acceptance required prior to backfill approval. Manhole vacuum test on all manholes. CCWRD inspection scheduled through CCWRD Plan Review Engineer's office (Vince Alarid, CCWRD).
[Normal] 5.2  Dry utilities (joint trench).
[Normal] Composite dry utility plan (electric — NV Energy; gas — Southwest Gas; telecom — CenturyLink and Cox) is on file. Joint trench and conduit installation to be sequenced by Mesquite Basin after storm drain and sewer are backfilled and prior to base course. Each dry utility purveyor will inspect its own facilities prior to trench closure. The dry utility coordinator will attend a joint trench pre-installation meeting on-site before joint trench work begins; date to be set by Mesquite Basin.
[Normal] 5.3  Locating existing.
[Normal] Blue-stake / USA North 811 will be called by Mesquite Basin for each work area 48 hours in advance of digging. Sundial will provide the contractor with the survey-verified locations of the offsite tie-ins at Rainbow Blvd.
[Normal] 5.4  Utility crossing conflicts.
[Normal] Any utility crossing conflict identified in the field will be reported by Mesquite Basin to Sundial the same day. Sundial will provide a resolution or field revision within 24 hours where possible; where a field revision affects an approved plan sheet, Sundial will issue a numbered field revision memo and copy the County construction inspector.
[Normal] 5.5  Fire protection features.
[Normal] Hydrant locations and fire department connections were walked by CCFD (Insp. Voight). Hydrant spacing on the plans meets CCFD standard. Hydrants are to be operational (flushed, tested, and flowed) prior to combustible construction commencing above the foundation on any dwelling unit. Hydrant flow test to be witnessed by CCFD and coordinated by Callaway's builder.
[Normal] 6.  Action Items Carried into Construction
[Normal] The following action list was compiled at the close of the meeting. Owners are named.

 DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS
                                 FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH

                          WITH COMMON AREA MAINTENANCE EXHIBIT

THIS DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH
(this "Declaration") is made and executed this 23rd day of December, 2024, by CALLAWAY LAND PARTNERS,
a Nevada limited liability company, having a principal place of business at 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400, Las
Vegas, NV 89148 (the "Declarant"), with reference to the facts recited below.



                                          ARTICLE I. RECITALS

A. Declarant is the owner in fee simple of certain real property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark
County, Nevada, being a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County,
Nevada, consisting of approximately 140.0 acres and commonly known and identified as the Desert Sage
Ranch subdivision (the "Property").

B. Declarant has caused the Property to be subdivided into three (3) sequential phases, being Phase 1, Phase
2, and Phase 3, together comprising residential lots, common-area parcels, streetscape parcels, and dedicated
public rights-of-way, all as more particularly depicted on the recorded final map(s) of the Property.

C. Concurrently with the execution and recordation of this Declaration, the First Final Map for Desert Sage
Ranch, Phases 1 and 2, being Map No. NFM-24-0118, is being recorded in the Office of the Clark County
Recorder at Book 175, Page 60 of Official Records ("First Final Map"). This Declaration is intended to be
recorded contemporaneously with, and to encumber the property depicted upon, the First Final Map, and to run
with and encumber the entire Property, including the Phase 3 remainder to be depicted on a successive final
map, upon its recordation.

D. It is the intention of Declarant to establish and impose upon the Property a general plan for the improvement,
protection, maintenance, and administration of Desert Sage Ranch as a planned residential community,
including without limitation the ownership and maintenance of certain common areas by a community
association formed for that purpose.
 E. Declarant intends that the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, assessments, charges, and liens
set forth below shall run with the land and be binding upon all persons or entities having or acquiring any right,
title, or interest in the Property or any portion thereof, and shall inure to the benefit of each Owner thereof.

F. Declarant has caused this Declaration to be prepared by Adrienne Vogel, Esq., of Vogel & Marsh LLP,
outside counsel to Declarant, in the manner set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, Declarant hereby declares that the Property shall be held, sold, conveyed, encumbered,
hypothecated, leased, used, occupied, and improved subject to the following covenants, conditions, restrictions,
easements, assessments, charges, and liens, all of which are declared to be in furtherance of a general plan
and scheme for the subdivision, improvement, and sale of the Property.



                                          ARTICLE II. DEFINITIONS

The following capitalized terms, when used in this Declaration, shall have the meanings set forth in this Article II.
Terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings customarily ascribed to them under Chapter 116 of
the Nevada Revised Statutes.

Section 2.1. "Articles." The Articles of Incorporation of the Association, as the same may be amended from
time to time.

Section 2.2. "Association." Desert Sage Ranch Community Association, a Nevada nonprofit corporation,
being the community association formed by Declarant to administer, own, and maintain the Common Area and
to enforce the terms of this Declaration. The Association is the community association contemplated by NRS
Chapter 116. All references herein to "HOA" mean the Association.

Section 2.3. "Board." The Board of Directors of the Association.

Section 2.4. "Bylaws." The Bylaws of the Association, as the same may be amended from time to time.

Section 2.5. "Common Area." All real property (including any Improvements thereon) that is (i) owned by the
Association in fee simple, or (ii) held by the Association under an easement, license, or maintenance obligation
for the common use and enjoyment of the Owners. Common Area expressly includes, without limitation, the
Common-Area Park, the Streetscape Common Area, the Entry Feature, and all landscaping, irrigation
infrastructure, hardscape, walls, monumentation, signage, and amenities located therein as installed by
Declarant or its successors. Common Area does not include any Lot or any portion of a public right-of-way
conveyed by dedication to Clark County or another public body.

Section 2.6. "Common-Area Park." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as
Parcel A, being an active-use park parcel improved with landscaping, irrigation, and, as installed by Declarant,
any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed, may consist of slides, swings, and climbing
structures). Parcel A is owned by the Association and is not part of any Lot.

Section 2.7. "Declarant." Callaway Land Partners, a Nevada limited liability company, and its successors and
assigns to whom the rights of Declarant hereunder are expressly assigned in a recorded instrument.

Section 2.8. "Declaration." This Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Desert Sage
Ranch, together with all exhibits and attachments hereto and all amendments and supplements duly recorded.
 Section 2.9. "Entry Feature." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as Parcel C,
being the community entry treatment situated at the intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, and
improved with entry monumentation, signage, walls, planting, irrigation, and accent lighting. Parcel C is owned
by the Association and is not part of any Lot.

Section 2.10. "Governing Documents." This Declaration, the Articles, the Bylaws, and the rules and
regulations of the Association, each as the same may be amended from time to time, together with all recorded
exhibits, plats, and supplemental declarations.

Section 2.11. "Improvement." Any structure, wall, fence, monument, sign, tree, shrub, turf, planting, irrigation
line, playground amenity, path, hardscape, or other tangible thing installed upon or affixed to the land.

Section 2.12. "Lot." Each numbered residential lot depicted upon a recorded final map of the Property and
intended for the construction and occupancy of a single detached residential dwelling. Each Lot is a separately
conveyable parcel; no Lot includes any portion of any Common Area, and no Common Area is any part of any
Lot.

Section 2.13. "Managing Agent." The community management firm engaged by the Association pursuant to a
written management agreement to perform the day-to-day administration of the Association's affairs, including
the maintenance and replacement obligations set forth in Article V. As of the date of this Declaration, the
Managing Agent is Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company, having offices
at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120.

Section 2.14. "Map" or "Final Map." Any final subdivision map of any portion of the Property recorded in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder, including the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, recorded at Book
175, Page 60) and any successive final map for Phase 3.

Section 2.15. "Owner." The record holder of fee simple title to a Lot, excluding any person or entity holding title
solely as security for the performance of an obligation.

Section 2.16. "Property." All of the real property described in Article III below and shown upon the Map(s),
together with all Improvements thereon, and any additional property annexed hereto in accordance with this
Declaration.

Section 2.17. "Streetscape Common Area." Those parcels or strips of Common Area situated between the
back-of-curb of a public street and the front or side lot lines of the adjoining Lots (or, where applicable, between
the back-of-curb and a perimeter community wall), extending along all frontage of the Property, and improved
with sidewalks (where the sidewalk is not within the dedicated public right-of-way), desert planting, street trees,
and drip irrigation. Each Streetscape Common Area parcel is owned by the Association and is not part of any
Lot.



                                ARTICLE III. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION

Section 3.1. Legal Description of the Property. The Property subject to this Declaration is that certain real
property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark County, State of Nevada, more particularly described as
follows:

       A portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County, Nevada,
       containing approximately 140.0 acres, together with all easements, tenements, hereditaments, and
       appurtenances thereunto belonging, commonly known as Desert Sage Ranch, situated at the
       intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las Vegas, Nevada 89178.
 Section 3.2. Phasing. The Property is subject to development in three sequential phases:

(a) Phase 1 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area, and dedicated street
rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

(b) Phase 2 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area (including the Common-Area
Park designated Parcel A, the shared Detention Facility designated Parcel B, and the Entry Feature designated
Parcel C), and dedicated street rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

(c) Phase 3 — that portion of the Property consisting of approximately 40.0 acres, presently identified by Clark
County Assessor's Parcel Number 177-27-201-001, to be subdivided into approximately sixty (60) half-acre
residential Lots, together with associated streetscape Common Area and dedicated street rights-of-way, all to be
depicted upon a successive final map to be recorded by Declarant. Upon recordation of the Phase 3 final map,
the Lots and Common Area created thereby shall automatically be and become subject to this Declaration
without the necessity of any further instrument.

Section 3.3. Annexation of Successive Phases. Declarant reserves the right, exercisable in its sole discretion
and without the consent of any Owner, Mortgagee, or the Association, to annex Phase 3 (and any lawful
reconfiguration thereof) to the regime of this Declaration by recordation of a Supplemental Declaration in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder that (i) identifies the annexed property by reference to the recorded final
map, and (ii) states that the annexed property is thereby made subject to this Declaration.

Section 3.4. Public Rights-of-Way. All streets, alleys, and other public rights-of-way depicted upon any Map
are conveyed by dedication to Clark County or the applicable public body. No such dedicated area is Common
Area, and the Association bears no maintenance obligation for improvements accepted for public maintenance
within any such dedicated area, except as provided by written agreement with the applicable public body.



                                     ARTICLE IV. COMMON AREAS

Section 4.1. Establishment of Common Area. Declarant hereby establishes and dedicates for the common
use and enjoyment of the Owners, and conveys to the Association concurrently herewith and by the recordation
of each applicable Map, all Common Area, in fee simple, free and clear of all monetary encumbrances other
than the lien of current taxes and assessments not yet delinquent and matters of record specifically noted upon
the Map.

Section 4.2. Parcel A — Common-Area Park. The parcel designated Parcel A on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Common-Area Park. Parcel A is owned in fee simple
by the Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel A is improved by Declarant with landscaping, irrigation, and,
as installed by Declarant, any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed by Declarant, may
consist of slides, swings, and climbing structures). All landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting,
hardscape, and playground amenities installed upon Parcel A, as and where installed, constitute Common Area
Improvements owned by the Association.

Section 4.3. Parcel C — Entry Feature. The parcel designated Parcel C on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Entry Feature. Parcel C is owned in fee simple by the
Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel C is improved by Declarant with community entry monumentation,
community identification signage, decorative perimeter walls, drip-irrigated desert planting, and accent lighting.
All Improvements installed upon Parcel C constitute Common Area Improvements owned by the Association.
 Section 4.4. Streetscape Common Area. The streetscape strips depicted on each recorded Map along all
frontage of the Property, being situated between the back-of-curb of the adjoining public street and the front or
side lot lines of the abutting Lots (or the adjoining perimeter wall, where applicable), are hereby established as
Streetscape Common Area. Each such strip is owned in fee simple by the Association, is not part of any Lot,
and is improved by Declarant with street trees, drip-irrigated desert planting, decorative rock cover, and, where
applicable, community perimeter wall and sidewalk. The Streetscape Common Area extends continuously along
the entire street frontage of the Property, in the extent depicted upon the First Final Map and upon any
successive final map recorded for Phase 3.

Section 4.5. Distinct from Lots. The Common-Area Park (Parcel A), the shared Detention Facility (Parcel B),
the Entry Feature (Parcel C), and each Streetscape Common Area parcel are each Common Area owned and
maintained by the Association, and no such parcel is a Lot or any part of a Lot. No Owner has any right, by
virtue of ownership of a Lot, to construct, remove, alter, replace, or reconfigure any Improvement located within
any Common Area.

Section 4.6. Easements Appurtenant. Every Owner shall have a nonexclusive easement of use and
enjoyment in and to the Common Area, appurtenant to and passing with title to such Owner's Lot, subject to the
terms of this Declaration and the rules and regulations of the Association.

Section 4.7. Reserved Easements. Declarant reserves to itself, the Association, the Managing Agent, and their
respective employees, agents, and contractors, a perpetual easement over, upon, across, and through each
Common Area parcel for the purposes of installing, inspecting, maintaining, repairing, and replacing Common
Area Improvements, including without limitation landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting, and
playground amenities, as installed.

Section 4.8. No Partition. The Common Area shall remain undivided. No Owner or other person shall bring any
action for the partition or division of the Common Area, and each Owner waives any right of partition such
Owner may hold at law or in equity.



                         ARTICLE V. MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT

Section 5.1. Association Responsibility. The Association shall be responsible for the continuous and ongoing
maintenance, repair, and replacement of the Common Area and all Improvements located thereon, including
without limitation:

(a) all landscaping within the Common Area, including all turf, planting, groundcover, shrubs, and trees, as and
where installed;

(b) all irrigation infrastructure within the Common Area, including without limitation mainline, laterals, valves,
valve boxes, backflow prevention assemblies, controllers, wiring, and emitters;

(c) all playground amenities located within the Common Area, as installed, including without limitation slides,
swings, climbing structures, and any associated resilient surfacing, safety zone materials, and containment
curbing;

(d) all hardscape within the Common Area, including sidewalks (where not within a dedicated public right-of-way
accepted for public maintenance), walls, monumentation, signage, benches, and accent lighting; and

(e) all other Improvements installed within the Common Area from time to time by Declarant or the Association.
 Section 5.2. Delegation to Managing Agent. The Association hereby delegates the day-to-day performance of
the maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations set forth in Section 5.1 to its Managing Agent, being, as of
the date of this Declaration, Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company
having offices at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120. The Managing Agent shall perform
such obligations pursuant to and in accordance with the written management agreement entered into between
the Association and the Managing Agent (the "Management Agreement"), which Management Agreement may
be renewed, replaced, or terminated by the Board in accordance with its terms and applicable law.

Section 5.3. Scope of Managing Agent Obligation. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the
Managing Agent is charged with and shall perform, in the name and on behalf of the Association:

(a) all routine and non-routine maintenance, repair, and replacement of the landscaping within all Common Area
parcels, including any turf, any planting, and any irrigation infrastructure, as and where installed by Declarant or
subsequently installed by or on behalf of the Association;

(b) the maintenance, repair, and replacement of all playground amenities located within any Common Area
parcel, as and where installed, including inspection for safety compliance and the replacement of resilient
surfacing and impact-attenuating materials;

(c) the procurement, supervision, and payment of qualified landscape maintenance contractors, irrigation
service contractors, playground safety inspectors, and other trades as required to discharge the foregoing
obligations;

(d) the maintenance of records of all such maintenance, repair, and replacement work; and

(e) periodic reporting to the Board with respect to the condition of the Common Area and any recommended
capital repair or replacement work.

Section 5.4. Assessments; Funding. The costs of performing the obligations set forth in this Article V shall be
borne by the Association and funded through regular and, if required, special assessments levied against the
Lots in accordance with this Declaration, the Bylaws, and NRS Chapter 116. The Managing Agent shall
administer the collection and application of such assessments in accordance with the Management Agreement.

Section 5.5. Owner Obligation with Respect to Lots. Each Owner shall be responsible for the maintenance,
repair, and replacement of all Improvements located upon such Owner's Lot, and the Association shall have no
obligation to maintain any portion of any Lot. Nothing in this Article V shall be construed to place upon the
Association or the Managing Agent any obligation with respect to any Improvement located within any Lot.

Section 5.6. Standard of Maintenance. All Common Area Improvements shall be maintained in a first-class,
safe, sanitary, and attractive condition consistent with the standard originally installed by Declarant, and
consistent with all applicable laws, ordinances, and codes of Clark County, the State of Nevada, and the United
States.

Section 5.7. Right of Entry. The Association, the Managing Agent, and their respective employees, agents,
and contractors shall have the right at all reasonable times to enter upon the Common Area (and, upon prior
notice except in an emergency, upon any Lot to the extent necessary to reach the Common Area or to abate a
nuisance affecting the Common Area) for the purposes of performing the maintenance, repair, and replacement
obligations set forth in this Article V.



                                  ARTICLE VI. GENERAL PROVISIONS
 Section 6.1. Covenants Running with the Land. The covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements,
assessments, charges, and liens set forth in this Declaration shall run with and bind the Property, and shall inure
to the benefit of and be enforceable by the Declarant, the Association, and each Owner, and their respective
legal representatives, heirs, successors, and assigns.

Section 6.2. Term. The term of this Declaration shall be perpetual, subject to termination or amendment as
expressly provided herein and by NRS Chapter 116.

Section 6.3. Amendment. Except as otherwise expressly reserved to Declarant herein, this Declaration may be
amended only by the affirmative vote or written consent of Owners representing not less than sixty-seven
percent (67%) of the total voting power of the Association, and shall be effective upon recordation of the
amendment in the Office of the Clark County Recorder.

Section 6.4. Enforcement. Enforcement of this Declaration shall be by any proceeding at law or in equity by the
Association, Declarant, or any Owner against any person or entity violating or attempting to violate any provision
hereof, either to restrain violation or to recover damages, or both. Failure by the Association, Declarant, or any
Owner to enforce any provision hereof shall in no event be deemed a waiver of the right to do so thereafter.

Section 6.5. Severability. Invalidation of any one of these covenants or restrictions by judgment or court order
shall not affect any other provisions, which shall remain in full force and effect.

Section 6.6. Governing Law. This Declaration shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws
of the State of Nevada, including without limitation NRS Chapter 116.

Section 6.7. Notices. Any notice required or permitted to be given to any Owner under this Declaration shall be
deemed to have been properly given when delivered personally or when deposited in the United States mail,
postage prepaid, addressed to the Owner at the mailing address for such Owner on file with the Association.

Section 6.8. Conflict. In the event of any conflict between this Declaration and the Articles or the Bylaws, this
Declaration shall control. In the event of any conflict between this Declaration and any applicable provision of
NRS Chapter 116 that cannot be varied by agreement, the statute shall control.

Section 6.9. Successors of Managing Agent. The identity of the Managing Agent may be changed from time
to time by the Board without the necessity of any amendment to this Declaration; provided that, at all times, the
maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations set forth in Article V shall be performed by the Association
directly or by a qualified Managing Agent engaged by the Association.

1. Executive Summary

This Geotechnical Investigation was performed at the proposed Desert Sage Ranch residential subdivision, a
140 acres master-planned community to be developed by Callaway Land Partners in three sequential phases
(Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3) within unincorporated Enterprise, Clark County, Nevada. The site is bounded
generally by Rainbow Boulevard to the west and Windmill Lane to the south, with undeveloped and partially
developed parcels to the north and east.

The subsurface exploration program consisted of twenty-four (24) hollow-stem-auger borings drilled between
September 13 and September 24, 2021, ranging in depth from 21.5 to 30.0 feet below existing grade, distributed
as approximately eight borings within each phase area. Six (6) infiltration tests were performed at basin-invert
candidate elevations to support drainage design. Selected samples were subjected to laboratory testing
including moisture-density, mechanical grading, Atterberg limits, expansion index, and soluble
sulfate/chloride/resistivity/pH corrosivity screening.

Key findings:
     • Native soils across the site consist predominantly of Holocene alluvial fan deposits mapped as silty sand
    (SM) and clayey sand (SC), grading with depth into weakly to strongly cemented caliche horizons typically
    encountered between 4 and 8 feet below existing grade.
    • Below the caliche horizon, dense to very dense silty sand with gravel and cobbles was encountered to the
    maximum depths explored.
    • Groundwater was not encountered in any boring to a depth of 30 feet. Historically high groundwater is
    estimated to be more than 100 feet below existing grade in this portion of the valley.
    • Expansion indices are low (EI < 20 on all samples tested); the surficial soils are non-expansive.
    • Corrosion screening indicates the native soils are moderately corrosive to buried ferrous metals and
    negligibly corrosive to concrete.
    • Infiltration rates measured across six test locations range from 1.8 to 6.2 inches per hour in the upper silty
    sand horizon and are considered favorable for surface retention/detention basin infiltration provided any
    indurated caliche crust at the basin invert is over-excavated and replaced with select granular material.

The site is considered suitable for the proposed single-family residential development from a geotechnical
standpoint. Conventional spread footings founded on properly prepared and compacted engineered fill are
recommended for support of the residential structures. Pavement sections are provided herein for light-duty
residential streets and heavy-duty collector streets.

The following sections and appendices provide the detailed basis of these conclusions.



                                             2. Site Description


2.1 Location and Setting

The Desert Sage Ranch site occupies approximately 140 acres in Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60
East, Mount Diablo Meridian, within the Enterprise planning area of unincorporated Clark County, Nevada. The
property is bounded by Rainbow Boulevard on the west, Windmill Lane on the south, existing single-family
residential to the east, and vacant county-owned land to the north.
