Terrain slopes generally from north to south at approximately 1.5% to 2.5%, with a shallow desert wash
traversing the southeastern portion of the site.



2.5 Soils

Per the Geotechnical Investigation Report of record for the property, native soils consist predominantly of silty
sand (SM) and poorly graded sand with silt (SP-SM), with intermittent caliche layers encountered between
approximately 3 and 10 feet below existing grade. Infiltration testing indicates moderate to low infiltration rates.
Boring logs and pavement recommendations are contained in the referenced geotechnical report.

Soil erodibility for the site is rated moderate. Wind erosion potential is elevated during periods of active
disturbance and dry, windy conditions typical of the Las Vegas Valley; dust control BMPs are implemented in
coordination with the site's Clark County dust control permit.



2.6 Receiving Water and Discharge Point

Stormwater from the site historically sheet flows to a regional dry-wash conveyance — an unnamed dry wash
traversing the southeastern portion of the site that is tributary to a regional flood control facility owned and
operated by the Regional Flood Control District. The ultimate downstream water body is the Las Vegas Wash.

During construction, stormwater will exit the site via sheet flow controlled by perimeter BMPs and, on completion
of the on-site detention basin (Phase 3 southern portion), via controlled release through the project outfall into
the dry-wash conveyance. The immediate receiving reach is not listed on the current Nevada 303(d) list of
impaired waters. Discharge routes through the Clark County / Regional Flood Control District system (MS4
discharge — Yes).



2.7 Impervious Cover

    • Existing (pre-construction): less than 1%
    • Developed (at buildout): approximately 45% (roofs, streets, driveways)


2.8 Site Map

A site plan is included as Attachment A. The site plan shows the following, at a minimum:

    • The full 140-acre project boundary,
    • The three phase boundaries (Phase 1 north; Phase 2 central; Phase 3 south),
    • Existing topography, drainage patterns and the dry-wash conveyance,
     • Location of all BMPs referenced in Section 5, by phase area,
    • Concrete washout, materials storage and equipment staging areas,
    • Stabilized construction entrance locations,
    • Detention basin location and project outfall,
    • Adjacent public rights-of-way and abutting land uses.



                             3. Sequence of Major Construction Activities

Construction of the 140-acre Desert Sage Ranch will proceed by phase, generally from north to south, and
generally in the sequence set out below. Each phase will follow a similar internal sequence of clear/grub →
mass grading → dry and wet utilities → street subgrade and paving → vertical construction (residential lots) →
final stabilization.



3.1 Overall Project Sequence (three phases)

    Pre-construction activities. Notice of Intent and SWPPP; NDEP coverage under NVR100000; Clark
    County grading, dust control and off-site permits; utility company coordination; installation of initial perimeter
    BMPs at the active phase boundary.
    Phase 1 — approximately 45 acres, north portion. Initial mass grading, arterial connection to Rainbow
    Boulevard, primary storm drain trunk, wet and dry utility mains, interior street subgrade, interim stabilization
    of pads pending vertical construction.
    Phase 2 — approximately 55 acres, central portion. Interior streets, wet and dry utilities, lot grading,
    tie-in to Phase 1 utilities and streets, interim stabilization, vertical construction on Phase 1 lots proceeds in
    parallel.
    Phase 3 — approximately 40 acres, south portion. Interior streets, wet and dry utilities, lot grading, final
    grading of the regional detention basin at the southern outfall, vertical construction on Phase 2 lots in
    parallel.
    Final stabilization, project-wide. Hydroseeding of disturbed common-area slopes; landscape installation
    in common areas and per-lot as vertical construction completes; removal of temporary BMPs once
    vegetative cover is established; Notice of Termination filed on the applicable disturbed acreage when final
    stabilization is achieved.


3.2 Typical Per-Phase Activity Sequence

    Install perimeter silt fence, stabilized construction entrance and inlet protection at the active phase
    boundary.
    Clear and grub within the active phase.
    Rough mass grading and cut/fill balancing.
    Storm drain, sewer and water main installation.
    Dry utility (electric, gas, telecommunications) joint trench installation.
    Street subgrade preparation, aggregate base placement, curb and gutter.

Statutory Presentation Requirements

The applicant's attention is directed to NRS 278.360, which governs the presentation of final maps in a phased
subdivision, the substance of which is summarised below:

       "A final map presented for recordation as the first map in a series must be presented to the
       governing body within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative
       map. Each successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the
       date on which the immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map
       terminates all proceedings relating to the subdivision. The governing body may, upon written
       application filed after the applicable period has expired, grant an extension of not more than two (2)
       years."

The applicant is on notice that the four-year and two-year periods described above run from the events identified
in the statute, not from any calendar reference stated by staff. Extensions of not more than two (2) years may be
sought only by written application filed after the applicable period has expired, and are discretionary with the
governing body. Nothing in this letter, and no informal communication from staff, shall be construed to extend,
waive, or modify the statutory deadlines.



                                       CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL


A. Public Works — Development Review (Conditions 1 through 10)

    Improvement plans for all phases shall be prepared by a professional engineer registered in the State of
    Nevada in accordance with the Clark County Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings for Public
    Works Construction and the Clark County Design and Construction Standards, current edition at the time of
    submittal.

    A drainage study, prepared in accordance with the Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic
    Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, shall be submitted with the first improvement plan submittal for each
    phase and shall demonstrate conformance with all applicable accepted district studies. Any proposed
    deviation from district-accepted parameters shall be resubmitted for district re-review prior to improvement
    plan approval.

    Right-of-way dedications and easements shown on the tentative map, including all public utility easements,
    drainage easements, and non-vehicular access easements, shall be granted by the recorded final map for
    the phase in which the affected area lies.

    Full half-street improvements shall be constructed along all abutting collector and arterial streets adjacent to
    the phase being platted, including curb, gutter, sidewalk, pavement, streetlights, signing and striping, in
    accordance with the applicable cross-section.
    Internal streets shall be constructed to Clark County local-street standards. Cul-de-sac dimensions,
   knuckles, and turning radii shall satisfy the requirements of both Public Works and the Clark County Fire
   Department.

   Sight visibility triangles shall be shown on the improvement plans and the landscape plans at every
   intersection and driveway. Landscaping, signage, and walls within the sight visibility zone shall comply with
   Section 30.52.025 (Sight Zones) of the Clark County Code.

   A traffic impact analysis shall be provided at the improvement plan stage for any phase, or portion of a
   phase, whose lot count, trip generation, or access configuration differs from the assumptions used in the
   tentative map traffic study. Off-site mitigation, if warranted, shall be constructed or bonded as a condition of
   the applicable final map.

   Prior to recordation of any final map, the applicant shall furnish a performance bond, cash-in-lieu, or other
   security acceptable to the Director of Public Works in the full amount of the engineer's estimate of probable
   cost of the public improvements associated with that phase.

   Final acceptance of public improvements for each phase shall be by written notice of acceptance from the
   Director of Public Works following completion of the two-year maintenance period and the punch-list walk.
   Bond release, in whole or in part, shall be governed by the terms of the applicable security instrument and
   shall not occur automatically.

   Construction stormwater discharges shall be authorized under the current Nevada Department of
   Environmental Protection general permit (NVR100000) prior to the commencement of grading. A Notice of
   Intent shall be filed and a Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan implemented for the duration of
   construction, and a Notice of Termination shall be filed upon final stabilization.


B. Clark County Fire Department (Conditions 11 through 13)

   Fire apparatus access roads, hydrant locations, hydrant flow, and required fire flow shall be shown on the
   improvement plans and shall comply with the International Fire Code as amended and adopted by Clark
   County. Secondary emergency access shall be provided in accordance with the Fire Code, and any
   secondary access designated as temporary shall be identified as such on the plans with the expiration event
   stated.

   Water mains and appurtenances serving fire hydrants shall be operational and accepted, and required fire
   flow shall be demonstrated by flow test, prior to combustible construction on any lot within the affected
   phase.

   Street names, address ranges, and access gate details (if any) shall be submitted for Fire Department
   review concurrently with the improvement plan submittal. Access codes to any gates restricting emergency
   access shall be provided to the Clark County Fire Department and the Metropolitan Police Department prior
   to activation.


C. Comprehensive Planning (Conditions 14 through 20)

   Any significant change to approved plans, including but not limited to landscape and streetscape
   treatments in common areas, shall be subject to design review as a public hearing before the
   applicable Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission prior to staff-level action.

   The final map(s) shall conform to the tentative map as approved, including lot count, lot geometry, phase
   boundaries, public street alignments, common-area boundaries, and dedications. Modification to any of the
    foregoing at the final map stage that is not the result of a routine survey adjustment shall be treated as a
   significant change under Condition 14.

   Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions (CC&Rs) establishing a homeowners association, defining
   common-area maintenance obligations, and identifying the party responsible for ongoing maintenance of
   streetscapes, park parcels, entry features, walls, and drainage facilities not accepted by the County, shall be
   recorded concurrently with the final map for the applicable phase. A common-area maintenance exhibit shall
   be attached to the CC&Rs.

   All identification signage, entry monumentation, and community features shall be shown on the landscape
   plans and shall be subject to Comprehensive Planning review prior to installation. Off-premise signage is
   not authorized by this approval.

   Lighting on streetscape, park parcels, and entry features shall be full cut-off and shall comply with the
   outdoor lighting standards of the Clark County Code. Photometric plans shall be provided with the
   improvement plan submittal for common-area lighting.

   Model home complexes, sales trailers, and temporary construction offices are not authorized by this
   approval. Separate permits shall be obtained through this Department prior to the establishment of any such
   use.

   This approval does not vest zoning, use, or development standards beyond those in effect on the date of
   approval. Nothing herein exempts the applicant from compliance with subsequently adopted regulations that
   apply to actions taken after the effective date of those regulations, including but not limited to landscape and
   water conservation standards.


D. Utilities (Conditions 21 through 24)

   A will-serve letter from the Las Vegas Valley Water District for domestic water and fire flow service to the
   phase being platted shall be current at the time of final map recordation. The applicant shall be responsible
   for maintaining currency of the will-serve; a lapsed will-serve shall be re-issued prior to recordation.

   A capacity confirmation from the Clark County Water Reclamation District for wastewater collection and
   treatment capacity for the phase being platted shall be current at the time of final map recordation. Sewer
   capacity confirmations are issued by the District under a separate schedule from water will-serve letters and
   are subject to their own expiration terms; the applicant is responsible for verifying currency independently.

   Dry utility joint-trench alignment shall be coordinated with the electric, natural gas, and telecommunications
   purveyors. A composite dry utility plan shall be submitted with the improvement plans, and joint trench
   easements shown on the final map shall reflect the composite plan as coordinated.

   Backflow prevention, meter sizing, and cross-connection control shall comply with the requirements of the
   Las Vegas Valley Water District and the Southern Nevada Health District.

TOKEN = re.compile(r"(\*\*|\^\{[^}]*\}|_\{[^}]*\})")


def add_runs(p, text, bold=False, size=None, italic=False, color=None):
    """Add text with light markup: **bold**, ^{sup}, _{sub}."""
    b = bold
    for part in TOKEN.split(text):
        if not part:
            continue
        if part == "**":
            b = not b
            continue
        sup = part.startswith("^{")
        sub = part.startswith("_{")
        if sup or sub:
            part = part[2:-1]
        r = p.add_run(part)
        r.bold = b
        r.italic = italic
        if size:
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color is not None:
            r.font.color.rgb = color
        if sup:
            r.font.superscript = True
        if sub:

    return p

    p = doc.add_paragraph()

    if after is not None:
        pf.space_after = Pt(after)
    if before is not None:
        pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep:

    if indent is not None:

    return p

              Adequacy and Disposition


1. Purpose and Bottom Line
Public Works comment G-4 (Dale Yeoman, PE, Ph3 Comments, 10/09/2026) reads: “The emergency
spillway shown on Sheet C-9 lacks freeboard dimensioning and downstream apron details. Provide sizing
calculations, spillway section, and erosion protection consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and
Drainage Design Manual.” Before the response is assigned, we checked the spillway as drawn against
the Phase 3 improvement plans and our internal QA/QC checklist, the District-accepted Master Drainage
Study (MDS) and the Phase 3 storm drain worksheets, and the Phase 2 plan check comments and the
Flood Control District’s acceptance letter. Records and their short names are listed in Attachment C.
The spillway as drawn does not hold up. Before the berm overtops it can pass 30.454425 cfs —
34.450707 % of the 88.4 cfs it must carry — and whatever it does pass lands on two residential lots. The
fix stays inside the accepted MDS, so it does not go back to the District and does not move the schedule.
One disposition per question follows; findings are in Sections 3 through 6, the arithmetic in Attachment A,
and draft sheet language in Attachment B. Elevations are feet, NAVD 88 (C-1, Datum note).

2. Dispositions
No.    Question                          Disposition
1      Can we answer G-4 with what is    No. There is no sizing anywhere in the record; the C-9 freeboard figures are wrong; the

                                         C-9 and C-6 are reissued (Section 3).

3      What do the spillway detail and   Spillway moved to the south berm; crest held at 2,858.50 ft; crest lengthened from 20.0
       basin notes say on the revised    ft to 50.0 ft; design discharge 88.4 cfs with the outlet blocked; design water surface
       C-9?                              2,859.27 ft; top of berm raised 1.10 ft to 2,860.30 ft for 1.03 ft of freeboard; armor

4      Where does the overflow end up Today: on private Lots 51 and 57. On the revised C-9 it leaves the south berm, runs
       once it leaves the berm?       in a lined channel on HOA land and a drainage easement to the Windmill Lane right-of-

          Garrett Nokes, Callaway Land Partners · Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 · Comment G-4, Emergency Spillway · 10/31/2026

Schedule. The redesign needs no District re-review, so it fits the dates already set: revised sheets to me
by 11/13/2026 (10/09/2026 coordination e-mail), internal completion 11/22/2026 and resubmittal
11/30/2026 (Tracker). Two things would put the 12/18/2026 recordation at risk: carrying the preliminary
calculation into the resubmittal, which is a formal amendment with District re-review before plan approval
(FCD Acceptance Letter; TM COA Condition 2), or moving the Parcel E line to make room for the raised
berm, which is a significant change requiring Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission hearings
(TM COA Conditions 14 and 15). This memo rules out both.

3. The Spillway as Drawn
3.1 No sizing exists anywhere in the record. The C-9 spillway detail gives no design discharge — only
“routing check under storm exceeding 100-year, 24-hour input.” MDS App. D-2 stops at the crest
(2,858.50 ft, 7.12 ac-ft, 41.5 cfs of outlet-works discharge) and shows no discharge at the 2,859.20-ft top
of berm. Neither the Hydrology Worksheet nor the HGL Worksheet contains a spillway rating. There is no
calculation on file to give Public Works.
3.2 The C-9 freeboard figures contradict the sheet’s own elevations. With the 100-year water
surface at 2,857.91 ft, the crest at 2,858.50 ft and the top of berm at 2,859.20 ft (C-6; C-9), the crest is
0.59 ft above the 100-year water surface. The C-9 spillway detail says 0.71 ft and the C-9 Basin Notes
say 0.60 ft. The 0.70-ft crest-to-berm and 1.29-ft water-surface-to-berm figures are correct, but the 1.29 ft
applies only with the outlet working and says nothing about freeboard while the spillway runs — which is
what G-4 asks us to dimension (Attachment A-1).
3.3 The spillway carries about one-third of its design flow before the berm overtops. We size an
emergency spillway on the standard basis — the 100-year peak inflow with the outlet works blocked —
which is 88.4 cfs for Phase 3 (MDS App. C-2 and D-1; Hydrology Worksheet, Peak Flows tab, cell B13).
With 0.70 ft of head between crest and berm, the 20.0-ft broad-crested weir (C-6; C-9) passes 30.454425
cfs at C = 2.6 ft0.5/s, 34.450707 % of the design discharge. Even at the theoretical ceiling for a broad
crest, C = 3.088809 ft0.5/s, it passes 36.179962 cfs, 40.927559 %. Carrying 88.4 cfs over the 20.0-ft crest
takes 1.424402 ft of head — a water surface of 2,859.924402 ft, 0.724402 ft over the berm. That holds
even if no freeboard were required at all (Attachment A-2).
3.4 No crest length produces freeboard with the berm where it is. The record’s minimum freeboard
is 1.0 ft (C-9 Basin Notes), and on Phase 2 Public Works required it “above the design HGL” and
dimensioned (Ph2 Comments, G-3, 09/28/2022, resolved 12/14/2022; Ph2 Response Matrix,
11/07/2022). For the spillway the design water surface is the crest plus the design head, so with the crest
held at 2,858.50 ft the berm must stand at 2,859.50 ft plus the head. The 2,859.20-ft berm is at least 0.30
ft short however long the crest is made. The berm has to go up (Attachment A-3).
3.5 The apron stops short of the toe and is not detailed. C-9 calls for a 15-ft by 20-ft grouted riprap
apron, D50 = 12 in, “extending from weir toe to natural grade beyond the berm at elevation 2,853.00′.” The
5.50-ft fall from the crest to 2,853.00 ft on the 3H:1V exterior slope (C-6) runs 16.50 ft horizontally and
17.392527 ft along the slope. Read as starting at the downstream edge of the 6.0-ft crest, the 15-ft apron
ends 1.50 ft (horizontal) short of the toe and never reaches natural grade; read as starting at the toe, it
leaves the 17.392527-ft face unarmored. Either way the face-to-grade transition, where the energy is
dissipated, is unprotected. No layer thickness, bedding, filter, toe-down or edge key is shown, and there is
no spillway section (Attachment A-5).
3.6 The outlet as detailed does not reproduce the rating behind the 100-year water surface. The
crest’s 0.59-ft margin rests on the 2,857.91-ft water surface routed through the MDS App. D-2 rating,
which describes orifice-and-weir outlet works. C-9 details a single 12-in by 18-in orifice (centroid 2,851.50
ft) and no weir. At Cd = 0.60 (dimensionless) it releases 80.524019 % more than App. D-2 at 2,853.00 ft
and 34.459424 % less at 2,857.91 ft (18.285821 cfs against 27.9 cfs), and it cannot release the accepted
27.9-cfs peak at any stage below the crest (19.108846 cfs at 2,858.50 ft against 41.5 cfs); matching 27.9
cfs at 2,857.91 ft would take Cd = 0.915463, which no orifice plate achieves. Neither the 2,857.91-ft water
surface nor the 0.59-ft margin is demonstrated for the outlet as drawn. Public Works made us reconcile
the Phase 2 outlet detail to the study for the same reason (Ph2 Comments, G-2); this closes in the same
revision (Attachment A-6).

        Sundial Engineering & Survey · Job No. 2201-03 · G-4 Emergency Spillway Memo · 10/31/2026 · Page 2 of 13
            Garrett Nokes, Callaway Land Partners · Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 · Comment G-4, Emergency Spillway · 10/31/2026

3.7 Our worksheets and checklist do not support the detail. The HGL Worksheet (Inputs, cell B40)
bounds its tailwater check at 2,858.50 ft as “the highest water surface the basin can physically hold”; with
the spillway flowing the water surface is the crest plus the head, so that bound is low. The same
workbook (Pipe Schedule notes) relies on “the grouted rip-rap apron detailed on Sheet C-9” to take the
14.25-fps Line B discharge at S-15, which enters at the basin’s north face (Inputs, cell B36); that apron
belongs to the spillway, on the outside of the east berm. The QA/QC Checklist (08/18/2026, Tab 3)
cleared item 27 (spillway) on crest-elevation agreement only, item 28 on freeboard “matching,” item 29 for
a “basin outlet swale section” keyed to Section B-B/C-9 — which is the transverse basin section; C-9 has
no swale section — and item 26 by matching an orifice “diameter” (the C-9 orifice is a 12-in by 18-in
rectangle) to an “inflow-outflow rating” the HGL Worksheet does not contain. None of those items tested
capacity, the freeboard arithmetic or the overflow path, so the checklist’s “no open items in Tab 3” cannot
be cited in the response.

 reissued. The drainage lead’s assignment is the redesign defined in Sections 5 and 6, not a response

As drawn, the spillway is on the east berm (C-6; C-9). On the FM Check Print (Sheet 4), the east line of
Parcel E abuts residential Lots 51 and 57. C-9 assumes “natural grade beyond the berm at elevation
2,853.00′,” but Phase 3 grading sets the pads of Lots 39 through 60 at 2,862.0 ft to 2,868.0 ft, stepping
down toward the basin (C-7) — at least 3.50 ft above the crest. Water leaving the east berm drops into
the strip between the berm toe and the rear yards of Lots 51 and 57 and cannot continue east. If Parcel E
were a band of uniform width around the 293-ft by 195-ft top-of-berm line (C-6), its 2.04 ac would give
29.049164 ft; the drawn crest and exterior face use 22.50 ft of that, leaving 6.549164 ft beyond the toe
before the lot line (Attachment A-8). No swale, channel or easement for the overflow appears on C-6, C-9
or the map; the only drainage easement on the map is 15 ft along the west line of Parcel D (FM Check
Print, Sheet 3). The water’s route out is south along and across those rear yards and over the strip Sheet
4 labels “Line B storm drain corridor” — which the map makes neither a lot, nor part of Parcel E, nor an
easement — to Windmill Lane. The C-9 note that flow “spreads to downstream open swale in Common-
Area Parcel ‘E’ and exits at Windmill Ln. gutter line” describes a facility that is not drawn, and Public
Works comment G-6 (Ph3 Comments) already reports gutter spread that appears to exceed the half-
street criterion at the Windmill Ln./Desert Sage Pkwy. low point.

 leaves the south berm into the lined overflow channel inside Parcel E, crosses the Line B corridor strip
 inside a drainage easement in favor of the Association shown on the resubmitted FM-26-100290
 (giving the strip the status its label already implies; no lot line or Parcel E line moves), enters the
 Windmill Lane gutter through a curb-and-walk outlet in the Phase 3 half-street improvements (TM COA
 Condition 4) sized for 88.4 cfs, and flows west in Windmill Lane toward Rainbow Boulevard and the
 regional system at the southwest corner (MDS §2.1; §5.1). The spillway is positioned so the channel

steps.message:
I've saved the memo at `/filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx`, dated 10/31/2026 and addressed to Garrett Nokes. It runs 13 pages: a 7-page memo plus Attachments A (calculations), B (draft wording for the revised C-9) and C (list of records). Short answer: the spillway as drawn does not hold up.

1. **Can we answer G-4 with what's on the sheet today? No.**
   - **No sizing anywhere.** No record has a design flow or rating for the spillway.
   - **Freeboard figures are wrong.** C-9's own elevations put the crest 0.59 ft above the 100-year water surface. The detail says 0.71 ft and the basin notes say 0.60 ft.
   - **Far too small.** The design flow is 88.4 cfs, the Phase 3 100-year peak inflow with the outlet blocked (master study App. C-2/D-1). The 20-ft weir passes only 30.454425 cfs before the berm overtops (34.450707 %). Carrying 88.4 cfs would put the water 0.724402 ft over the berm.
   - **Freeboard is impossible as built.** The crest is only 0.70 ft below the top of berm. With the crest held, the berm is at least 0.30 ft short of the 1.0-ft freeboard minimum (the standard Public Works applied on Phase 2, comment G-3), however long the crest is made.
   - **Apron is short.** The 15-ft apron can't reach the toe; the slope length to natural grade is 17.392527 ft.
   - **Outlet doesn't match the master study.** The single 12×18-in orifice on C-9 gives 18.285821 cfs at the 100-year water surface, against 27.9 cfs in App. D-2.
   - **QA/QC didn't catch it.** Checklist items 26–29 cleared the detail without checking any of this.

2. **Do the revisions trigger an amendment? No.** The fix keeps every accepted master-study value: 6.4 ac-ft, the 78 cfs outfall cap, 40.0 ac at 42 % impervious, 88.4 cfs, the D-2 rating up to the 2,858.50-ft crest, and the basin in Parcel E. The 09/25/2026 preliminary detention calc (65 % impervious, 26.5 ac offsite, 6.0 cfs release, 8.1 ac-ft) breaks every one of those and would trigger an amendment, so the memo sets it aside.

3. **What the revised C-9 says.**
   - Spillway moves to the south berm; crest stays at 2,858.50 ft and lengthens to 50.0 ft.
   - Design water surface is 2,859.273284 ft; top of berm rises 1.10 ft to 2,860.30 ft, giving 1.026716 ft of freeboard.
   - Armor runs the full slope into a lined overflow channel; the outlet is redesigned to match App. D-2.
   - The basin notes are rewritten in full in Attachment B.

4. **Where the overflow goes.** Today it lands on private Lots 51 and 57. The Phase 3 map check print puts those lots on Parcel E's east line, and their pads (2,862 ft and up) sit above the crest, so the water can't continue east. Revised, it goes south through Parcel E and a drainage easement into Windmill Lane, then west. That street routing has to be checked together with Dale's comment G-6 on the Windmill Lane low point.

Things to confirm:
- **Signature block** is set up for Max Braddock as Project Manager; change it if you're signing under a different name.
- **Design basis** is my professional judgment, not a manual citation: blocked outlet, weir coefficient 2.6, and 1.0 ft of freeboard above the spillway water surface.
- **Parcel E fit:** raising the berm widens it 7.70 ft on each side. Neither the plans nor the map check print give enough dimensions to confirm it fits inside Parcel E. If it's tight, the memo says lengthen the crest. Don't lower the crest (that changes an accepted App. D-2 value) or move the Parcel E line, which would mean Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission hearings under the tentative-map conditions.
- **Client action:** Callaway's one item is a supplemental CC&R declaration. Parcel E isn't in the recorded maintenance exhibit even though the plan notes say it is.
